moat_against: Low end-customer switching costs — the installer/dealer owns the replacement decision
Trane extending its commercial lead; Carrier/Daikin match on efficiency and scale
Housing- and rate-sensitive earnings (residential volumes -12% YoY in Q2 2026)
R-454B refrigerant transition cost and share-loss risk; regulatory/tax-credit policy shifts
moat_for: Big-four oligopoly structure with rational pricing in North American HVAC
Premium residential brand and highest-tier efficiency ratings
Commercial/BCS share gains and national-account wins in 2026, plus bolt-on M&A breadth
Replacement-driven demand (~75% of residential sales) cushions new-construction cycles
moat_justification: Big-four North American HVAC oligopoly with premium brand, direct dealer network and proven pricing power — roic_proxy 33-52% over the last five fiscal years and gross margin up from 27-28% to 33.4% — but low end-customer switching costs, equally strong Trane/Carrier/Daikin rivals, housing cyclicality and R-454B transition risk keep it moderate, not wide.
name: Lennox International Inc
one_liner: High-quality HVAC oligopolist, moat 6/10 — but at $357.73 it does not clear 15% in any scenario (weighted IRR 8.3%, IV@15% $161.99); it would need to fall to ~$162 to clear the 15% hurdle.
